name: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Audit and Remediation
description: Benchmark scenario evaluating an agent's capability to audit a flawed web UI component hierarchy for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance defects and remediate them.
instructions:
Audit and remediate accessibility defects in the provided web components according to WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines:

1. Modal Dialog Remediation (`src/components/modal-dialog.ts`):
   - Add `role="dialog"` (or `role="alertdialog"`) and `aria-modal="true"` to the modal container element.
   - Ensure the modal is properly named using `aria-labelledby` referencing the modal title element id.
   - Implement keyboard focus trapping: when the modal is open, pressing `Tab` or `Shift+Tab` must cycle focus exclusively through focusable elements inside the modal without escaping to the background document.
   - Add an `Escape` key listener on `keydown` to dismiss the modal dialog.
   - Save the active element prior to opening, and restore focus to the originating trigger element upon dialog closure.

2. Accessible Form Remediation (`src/components/accessible-form.ts`):
   - Associate all form controls (`<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>`) with explicit `<label>` elements using `htmlFor` / `for` attributes matching input `id` values, or `aria-labelledby`.
   - Mark required inputs with `aria-required="true"` and/or `required`.
   - Provide dynamic error announcements by adding `aria-live="polite"` (or `role="alert"`) to form error containers.
   - Associate error messages with invalid controls using `aria-describedby` and set `aria-invalid="true"` on inputs with active validation errors.
   - Move keyboard focus to the first invalid field upon failed form submission.

3. Verification:
   - Ensure the automated accessibility checker in `src/a11y-checker.ts` passes.
   - Verify TypeScript compilation succeeds without errors.

judgeRubrics.name: WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance Depth
judgeRubrics.description: Evaluates the comprehensiveness and technical accuracy of WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility remediation across keyboard operability (2.1.1, 2.1.2), focus management (2.4.3), form labels and instructions (3.3.2), error identification and announcements (3.3.1, 4.1.3), and ARIA semantics (4.1.2).

criteria.1: Minimal or broken remediation. Essential ARIA roles, labels, and keyboard traps are missing or improperly configured, failing core WCAG AA requirements.
criteria.2: Incomplete accessibility implementation. Added basic markup or labels but missed keyboard traps, focus restoration, or dynamic error announcements.
criteria.3: Solid baseline WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. Dialog roles, modal attributes, form associations, and error alerts are present, though minor keyboard or focus edge cases remain.
criteria.4: High quality remediation with robust keyboard handling (Tab wrapping and Escape dismissal), complete accessible name associations, and live error announcements.
criteria.5: Exemplary WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. Flawless focus trap with boundary wrapping, initial focus placement, focus restoration to opener, aria-describedby error links, polite/assertive live regions, and semantic HTML.

judgeRubrics.name: Component Architecture and Hygiene
judgeRubrics.description: Evaluates component design, TypeScript type safety, DOM lifecycle management, event listener cleanup, and maintainability of the remediated accessible components.

criteria.1: Brittle DOM manipulation with memory leaks, unremoved event listeners, broken type definitions, or regressions in core component rendering.
criteria.2: Functional but poorly structured code with inconsistent event handling, unhandled edge cases, or loose typing.
criteria.3: Clean TypeScript implementation with proper event cleanup, structured component interfaces, and standard error handling.
criteria.4: Well-factored, modular component architecture with strong types, robust lifecycle management, and clear separation between presentation and accessibility logic.
criteria.5: Production-grade component design: strictly typed, zero memory leaks with comprehensive event listener disposal, modular accessibility hooks/helpers, and elegant code organization.
